doc.title: Holly Hofmann interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Who was first on a jazz record: Wayman Carver, Sam Most, Wess
summary: Rowe and Hofmann discuss the historical confusion over the first jazz flutist, and Wess's role in the Basie band.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. There seems to be a — let’s say historical confusion about who actually was the first, or at least flute player to appear on a jazz record. Some say it was Frank, I’ve heard Sam Most.
I think actually it was Wayman Carver.
Okay, that’s another name I’ve heard.
And really that was the first one. And shortly after that, Sam Most, Joe Farrell, Frank Wess. I’m not quite sure of the chronology there.
He really gave the Basie thing another sound to work with and inspired all those cool arrangements.
Oh, yeah. Those were the years of the Basie band.
